known.title: Not done: start refusals leave branches and worktrees untouched
Not done: retain the Forge-merged trailer in bounded merge bodies

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. The new stack refusal runs at line 282, after `start` may create a local `story/<key>` branch at lines 208–210, add its worktree at lines 214–219, and merge into it at line 228. In a checkout that has fetched an approved story but has no local story branch, starting B while A has not started creates that branch before reporting `base_not_started`. This violates item 2's requirement that each refusal happen before any branch or commit. The test creates its local story branch during setup, so its before-and-after ref check misses this case.
findings.title: Not done: start refusals leave branches and worktrees untouched

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. The trailer is appended before `close._bounded_body` runs. For a merge body over its 65,536-byte limit, that function can shorten the trailing `Proof list:` section through the end of the body or remove the unprotected `Forge-merged:` line during prose clipping (`src/forge/close.py:961–966, 980–1021`). The squash commit then lacks the trailer, so `forge_merged` returns empty and a reviewed stacked part remains blocked from becoming a base after Forge merged the lower part.
findings.title: Not done: retain the Forge-merged trailer in bounded merge bodies

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test. The named proof requires A to have started on the older Forge release before the client upgrades. Both parametrizations upgrade or configure the client before `reviewed(env)` starts A; the `older` case instead edits A's `forge.toml` after its review and pushes that edit. It proves a changed pin is refused, but cannot catch a regression specific to recognizing the state of a part genuinely started before upgrade.
findings.title: Not done: test an older base started before upgrade
